name: go-duplicate-same-dir-asks
desc: a new Go def whose name already exists in another file of the SAME package (dir) is a real collision → ask

name: go-duplicate-different-dir-clean
desc: same name in a DIFFERENT directory is an unrelated package symbol the compiler keeps distinct → no ask

name: go-duplicate-test-file-skipped
desc: test files legitimately reuse symbol names across files → the check skips an edited _test.go

name: go-duplicate-cross-language-clean
desc: a Go def sharing a name with a Python sibling is not a collision (separate namespaces) → no ask

name: go-duplicate-test-file-candidate-clean
desc: the new symbol also exists in a _test.go in the SAME directory — a table-driven test's helper, or a fake with the same name as the thing it fakes. Test files are excluded as duplicate CANDIDATES, which is a different rule from skipping edits TO a test file (the case above): here the edited file is production code and only the match is a test. Replaces go-duplicate-not-defined-elsewhere-clean, which caught no defect: with nothing enrolled under that name the check has nothing to find, so its silence was structural rather than a rule doing work
